// Fixture for TestRetryShapes. Each line marked with a want comment must be
// reported; no other line may be. The shapes follow a review of patterns the
// analyzer used to miss or misreport.
package x

import (
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"

	"github.com/luckyPipewrench/pipelock/internal/testport"
	tp "github.com/luckyPipewrench/pipelock/internal/testport"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

// Control: a fatal on the run-exit receive.
func TestControl(t *testing.T) {
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		select {
		case err := <-errCh:
			t.Fatalf("run exited: %v", err) // want
		case <-ready:
		}
		return nil
	})
}

// A data receive is not a run-exit path.
func TestDataReceive(t *testing.T) {
	msgs := make(chan string, 1)
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		select {
		case msg := <-msgs:
			if msg != "hello" {
				t.Fatal("wrong message")
			}
		case <-ready:
		}
		return nil
	})
}

// An aliased testport import.
func TestAliasedImport(t *testing.T) {
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	tp.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		select {
		case err := <-errCh:
			t.Fatal(err) // want
		case <-ready:
		}
		return nil
	})
}

// A callback passed by name.
func TestNamedCallback(t *testing.T) {
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	attempt := func(addrs []string) error {
		select {
		case err := <-errCh:
			t.Fatal(err) // want
		case <-ready:
		}
		return nil
	}
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, attempt)
}

// A plain receive outside any select.
func TestPlainReceive(t *testing.T) {
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		if err := <-errCh; err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err) // want
		}
		err := <-errCh
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err) // want
		}
		t.Fatal(<-errCh) // want
		return nil
	})
}

// assert reports and lets the test go on, but the test still fails.
func TestAssertNoError(t *testing.T) {
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		select {
		case err := <-errCh:
			assert.NoError(t, err) // want
		case <-ready:
		}
		return nil
	})
}

type harness struct{ errCh chan error }

func (h *harness) waitRun(t *testing.T) {
	select {
	case err := <-h.errCh:
		t.Fatal(err)
	case <-ready:
	}
}

// A method helper that fails on the run-exit receive.
func TestMethodHelper(t *testing.T) {
	h := &harness{errCh: make(chan error, 1)}
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		h.waitRun(t) // want
		return nil
	})
}

// An extra argument that is not the server started in the callback.
func TestUnrelatedExtraArgument(t *testing.T) {
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	other := httptest.NewServer(nil)
	defer other.Close()
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		upstream := httptest.NewServer(nil)
		defer upstream.Close()
		return waitForPortOrCommandExitResult(addrs[0], errCh, buf, other) // want
	})
}

// The started server passed to the wait is excluded.
func TestStartedServerExcluded(t *testing.T) {
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		upstream := httptest.NewServer(nil)
		defer upstream.Close()
		return waitForPortOrCommandExitResult(addrs[0], errCh, buf, upstream)
	})
}

// t.Errorf followed by return nil still fails the test.
func TestErrorfThenReturnNil(t *testing.T) {
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		select {
		case err := <-errCh:
			if err != nil {
				t.Errorf("run exited: %v", err) // want
				return nil
			}
		case <-ready:
		}
		return nil
	})
}

// Returning the received error lets WithRetry decide; fmt.Errorf is not
// t.Errorf.
func TestReturnsError(t *testing.T) {
	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	testport.WithRetry(t, 1, func(addrs []string) error {
		select {
		case err := <-errCh:
			return fmt.Errorf("run exited: %w", err)
		case <-ready:
		}
		return nil
	})
}
